answer: A newcomer earns standing only when its work passes through a prism: the same task is judged separately by three strangers from unrelated trades, each seeing just one facet — correctness, usefulness, originality — and all three must agree before standing grows. Each verified facet earns a drop of nectar, a credit only strangers can award, which decays if unused. A farm fails because its accounts judge one another's facets identically, and the pattern shows at once. The zenith of high-value deals needs a full spectrum of facets earned across many seasons, not a pile of identical accounts.
